gen-dafont-origami-gf-savate: Savate keeps its hairlines sturdy and its curves wide open, with a rounded o nearly the size of a capital. Origami does the loud thing, one brushed line of constant width; Savate does the quiet one, with fuller stems and slimmer links.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk has big, open-looking e and a shapes, with terminals that never close in. Schibsted Grotesk would carry a long page easily, approachable and unhurried, while Origami's ribbon-like strokes stay up top as the pair's one loud gesture.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sen: Tall lowercase traced in a single steady line gives Sen a modern, upright look, with curves that stop before turning inward. And Origami, a brush-signed display face, can take the spotlight while Sen's size is nudged up a touch for comfort.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sintony: Contemporary all the way through, this pairing puts a heavy-handed brush outline over something much lower-key. Origami's steady, unshaded strokes and Sintony's chunky, tall midzone make a combination that is smooth rather than fussy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sofia-sans: Modern and uncluttered, Sofia Sans has rounded letters with a clearly open side and no thick-and-thin modulation at all. And its lowercase stands tall like cut acrylic stencil pieces, so a long passage moves along smoothly beneath Origami's brush-painted heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sofia-sans-semi-co: Origami paints each letter in a single brushed stroke, with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. And Sofia Sans Semi Condensed answers in stencil-cut channels, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals, which makes the heading earn its keep when it runs big and short.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sono: Sono spaces its letters generously and stands its lowercase tall, each a left slightly ajar. Sono makes a relaxed, approachable read over a long page, while Origami's parallel-edged strokes sit above it like cut ribbon.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-stack-sans-headlin: A brushed single stroke of constant width, plus a lowercase mass like poured lead type, defines Origami. Stack Sans Headline does the careful work instead: wide gaps keep tiny sizes crisp, and its deep middle band and monoline skeleton stay tidy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-stack-sans-notch: Stack Sans Notch reads open and big-bodied, with curves you can see right into. Origami earns its keep when set big and short, its brush strokes against the rod-stock horizontals and verticals of the plain sans below.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-stack-sans-text: Origami draws everything with a sign-painter's single brush stroke, a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Stack Sans Text brings a marker-like line and big-bodied lowercase with curve endings kept well apart, so the pair's strongest quality is how much the two lines differ.
